Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: streaming-decode p99 spike in us-west-2. Alerts started at 2026-03-14T03:10Z. Impacting streaming endpoints (chat/stream) — elevated tail latencies and intermittent client timeouts. Pager to #eng-oncall. https://metrics.internal/redwood/alerts/streaming-decode-p99
Alex W: oncall here, taking. Any immediate mitigation recommended?
Jamie (SRE): seeing p95 ~ 320ms -> 450ms, p99 jumps to 2.1s. Tail spike correlates with kernel/compilepath rollout at ~03:08 UTC. Spike coincides with new TRT8/flashattn-linked kernels on a subset of nodes.
Priya M: I rolled the optimized compilepath (compile-id: cp-20260314-trt8-flash-patch) to canary pool at 03:05, full rollout started 03:09. Logs show increased pagefaults and repeated small KV cache evictions under streaming workloads. Suspect kernel memory layout change impacting decode hot paths.
Theo R (runtime): confirming. Streaming sessions show many short-lived allocations and a rise in device page faults; decode threads sometimes block on kernel memory map. I can collect a kernel stack sample.
Alex W: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop rollout / pause any further deploys, 2) route new streaming traffic to older pool, 3) roll back compilepath on canary nodes, 4) notify CS for customer comms. I'll start routing.
deploy-bot: route-update accepted: redirecting 40% of new streaming sessions from pool:canary-usw2 -> pool:stable-usw2. command id: r-1763510001
Jamie (SRE): adding graphs and traces: https://dashboards.internal/streaming/us-west-2?range=1h. I'm seeing error spikes (upstream timeouts) that line up with buffer eviction logs in engine.
Olivia CS: two customers (acme-inc, finlytics) reported increased client-side stalls and a few reconnects. They asked for ETA and workaround.
Priya M: can we gate by disabling continuous batching on canary? That reduces pressure on KV cache and may avoid the eviction pattern. Runtime flag: 
```
redwood-runtime --enable-continuous-batching=false --pool=canary-usw2
```
But that will increase per-token cost; it's a short-term mitigation.
Alex W: executing steps now: pausing rollout and disabling continuous batching on canary nodes. Rolling back cp-20260314-trt8-flash-patch on canary -> cp-20260307-stable.
Theo R (runtime): I'm pushing a temporary routing rule to send new short-seq (<256) requests to stable pool to avoid worst-case tails. CLI: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/reroute \ 
  -d '{"from":"canary-usw2","to":"stable-usw2","filter":"seq_len<256","weight":0.6}' \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Applied.
Jamie (SRE): after routing ~60s in, p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 700ms on stable nodes; canary still shows high tail but traffic reduced. This indicates the new compilepath was causing the majority of stalls.
Priya M: collecting kernel oops/stack traces from affected nodes and nvprof traces for TRT kernels. Early grep of dmesg shows repeated: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 79, GPU page fault at VA 0x7ff...
[  123.456800] redwood-runtime: handle_kv_eviction: eviction_count=342 seq=...
```
Not definitive but aligns with memory management change in the kernel module we shipped.
Alex W: communication: Olivia, do we want a short note to customers: "We've identified a performance regression impacting streaming latency in us-west-2 and are rerouting traffic to mitigate. Investigating kernel/compilepath rollback; ETA 30-45m." Send?
Olivia CS: yes, please. Include that we're prioritizing production traffic and engineers are on it. I'll send the note and collect any customer logs.
deploy-bot: rollback job started for cp-20260314-trt8-flash-patch -> cp-20260307-stable on nodes [canary-1..canary-24]. job id rb-1763510123
Jamie (SRE): monitoring: CPU/GPU utilization slightly higher on stable after routing but within capacity. p95 stabilized ~250ms across stable pool.
Priya M: quick root-cause hypothesis: a codegen change in the trt-flash path increased indirection in KV lookup, which combined with a kernel memory layout tweak triggers more page faults during streaming decode. Need binary diff of kernels and compile flags (GLIBC/ld?).
Theo R (runtime): can reproduce locally under a scaled emulator with cp-20260314-trt8-flash-patch + high concurrency; I can produce a small reproduction harness and perf traces. Assign me to collect perf.data and gdb stack samples.
Alex W: good. For now, keep routing rule in place and finish rollback. Priority: restore SLOs in us-west-2 (p99 < 1s target).
Jamie (SRE): rollback completed on canary nodes at 03:28 UTC. Metrics show p99 falling to ~480ms within 2m of rollback completion.
Olivia CS: customers updated. acme-inc replied they see improvement. finlytics still reported a couple reconnects but much better.
Alex W: closing the pager as mitigation effective. Follow-ups: 1) Priya & Theo to own root-cause and produce a postmortem (include binary diffs, compile flags, and perf traces), 2) engineering to add a pre-rollout streaming load test for compilepath changes, 3) SRE to add an automated canary gating rule to hold rollouts when p99 > 1s for >5m.
Priya M: ack, I'll start the RCA doc and tag runtime and trt teams.
Jamie (SRE): filing incident ticket: INC-20260314-1423, assigning to Priya; I'll attach dashboards and waveform captures.
Alex W: thanks everyone. If anything regresses, reopen here.
Incident Bot: Incident marked as mitigated by Alex W at 2026-03-14T03:35Z. Postmortem follow-up required.
